The project-local yarn cache does NOT need a vendor_dir: .yarnrc.yml sets enableGlobalCache false, so it lives at /src/.yarn/cache and rides along with the /src export.

source._source_prep_note:
THE BIT-FOR-BIT FIX (chain 479, 2026-10-04). Published sha256:3e1b6076... and the offline rebuild sha256:8fe7d602... differed in ONE layer (COPY --from=jbuild /usr/share/jenkins), in ONE file of it (jenkins.war; the 63 plugin .hpi files were identical), in ONE war entry (WEB-INF/lib/jenkins-core-2.580.1.jar), and inside that jar ONLY in which *.stapler resources exist: 6 present only in the published jar (e.g. hudson/model/Api/doXml.stapler), 6 only in the rebuild (e.g. hudson/security/csrf/CrumbIssuer/RestrictedApi/doXml.stapler) plus 2 directory entries. Every class, every other resource, every timestamp and the entry order were identical.

ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM, in stapler 2119's QueryParameterAnnotationProcessor (still on stapler master). It collects the @QueryParameter methods into a HashSet of javac symbols -- identity-hash order -- and then SKIPS a method when the last file written for the same SIMPLE method name had the same parameter names. The skip was meant for same-class StaplerRequest/StaplerRequest2 overloads but is keyed across classes, so of every group like Api.doXml / RestrictedApi.doXml or the ~10 AdminMonitor.doAct methods only the first in hash order gets its file. Identity hashes depend on everything the JVM did before (Maven's own work, the GC ergonomics the host's CPU count picks), so the set varies run to run and host to host: the vendor build, the publish and the rebuild all produced DIFFERENT sets (206/208/207 files), and two local control compiles of the same vendored tree (2 CPUs, 1 CPU) produced a fourth and fifth. No flag, epoch or pin reaches this; it is an ordering bug in a build tool.

THE FIX shadows that one class. The three commands above write an order-independent drop-in with the SAME fully qualified name (one .stapler per class+method path, the comparison-smallest names on a same-path clash, written from a sorted map), install it as dev.readystack.build:stapler-qp-deterministic:1 into /m2, and patch core/pom.xml to list it FIRST in annotationProcessorPaths -- javac's processor class loader searches the path in order, so stapler's own META-INF/services entry resolves to our class, while stapler's other two processors (ConstructorProcessor, ExportedBeanAnnotationProcessor; ExportedBean already sorts with a TreeSet) run untouched. It is a BUILD-TOOL change only: the stapler jar we ship in WEB-INF/lib is upstream's, untouched. It runs in source_prep, BEFORE the online build, so the vendored target/ and the offline replay agree whether or not Maven decides to recompile core (it does: 'Recompiling the module because of changed dependency'). The pom patch fails the vendor stage unless it inserted exactly one entry.

WHAT THE SHIPPED JAR GAINS: 224 .stapler files, a strict superset of every upstream build observed (union 219) -- the complete set upstream intended. They are inert at runtime either way: core compiles with -parameters and Stapler reads reflection names, then bytecode debug info, and only then a .stapler file (ClassDescriptor.loadParameterNames), which is why upstream never noticed half of them going missing. The jar's embedded META-INF/maven pom is the flattened one and does not change.

VERIFIED LOCALLY on the chain-479 vendored tree, offline, the same mvn command: patched compile on 2 CPUs (G1) and on 1 CPU (SerialGC, a different identity-hash stream) -> byte-identical jenkins-core jar (sha256 422f2e9a...); unpatched control on the same two settings -> two different jars. The patched jar differs from a control jar ONLY in .stapler entries and their two directory entries.

THE LAST COMMAND PINS GUAVA 33.7.2-jre IN THE BOM (chain 681 G8, 2026-10-27: REPUBLISH_REQUIRED, 'OSV cross-check: CVE-2026-102554 not counted by Scout'). jenkins-2.580.1's bom/pom.xml manages com.google.guava:guava at 33.7.1-jre, which core bundles as WEB-INF/lib/guava-33.7.1-jre.jar in jenkins.war -- the image's ONLY guava (the SBOM lists none in the 220 plugin packages). GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94 / CVE-2026-102554 (HIGH, published 2026-10-27): CompactHashMap/CompactHashSet/MapMakerInternalMap deserialization allocates without bound; fixed in 33.7.2-jre (released 2026-09-29). Upstream made the same change on master on 2026-10-01 (jenkinsci/jenkins#27459, 'Update dependency com.google.guava:guava to v33.7.2-jre'), after the 2.580 LTS line branched, so no LTS ships it yet. 33.7.2 is a pure patch release: guava-parent 33.7.1 and 33.7.2 declare the same failureaccess 1.0.3, listenablefuture 9999.0-empty, jspecify 1.0.1 and j2objc 3.1. It runs in source_prep, before the online build, so Maven resolves 33.7.2 into /m2 and the offline replay builds the same war. A retarget to an LTS that already manages >= 33.7.2 leaves the file as it is and passes; anything below 33.7.2 after the patch fails the vendor stage. Remove the command once the LTS bom carries 33.7.2 or later.

source._online_vendor_cmds_note:
THE FRONTEND BUILD IS NOT SKIPPABLE. pom.xml activates the yarn-execution profile on the mere existence of package.json, with no skip property wired, and jsbundles/ is gitignored and absent from the tag — no bundles, no UI. -Pquick-build drops spotless/spotbugs/checkstyle/tests/enforcer and the yarn LINT, but not the yarn BUILD, which is what we want.

Plugins: until 2026-11-02 upstream's jenkins-plugin-cli resolved the closure of the five named plugins from the war's own version at the update centre's newest releases; the closure is now pinned in source.vendor_closures[jenkins-plugins] (63 plugins, each by version and the update centre's sha256), downloaded before these commands run. Jenkins with no plugins cannot even clone a git repo, so an empty plugins/ would be a technically-Grade-A non-product.

NOTE the plugin .hpi files are third-party artefacts with their own licences — all OSI-approved for this set (the 19 'suggested' plugins close over 92, of which 76 are MIT), but they are NOT built from source by us and the archive documentation must say so.

THE SECOND COMMAND PATCHES ONE PREBUILT PLUGIN (chain 492 verdict, 2026-10-05: Scout fixable C/H=4). jackson2-api 2.22.2-445.vdc613f1d8012 bundles jackson-core and jackson-databind 2.22.2, which carry CVE-2026-89425, CVE-2026-89407 (core) and CVE-2026-91776, CVE-2026-91777 (databind), all HIGH, all fixed in 2.22.3 (published 2026-09-30/10-01). No jackson2-api release bundles 2.22.3 yet: upstream's bump is the unmerged dependabot PR jenkinsci/jackson2-api-plugin#351 (jackson-bom 2.22.2 -> 2.22.3), and Jenkins core bundles no Jackson at all, so neither a plugin pin nor a core dependencyManagement override can reach it. The command does what that PR would ship: it replaces all 13 bundled Jackson 2.22.2 jars in the vendored .jpi with upstream's 2.22.3 releases from Maven Central, each checked against a pinned sha256. 2.22.3 is a pure patch release (jackson-base/-dataformats-text/-binary POMs differ from 2.22.2 only in version and build timestamp; annotations stay 2.22 from jackson-annotations2-api). Every other entry of the plugin is kept byte for byte, manifest first, in upstream's order, with a fixed entry date, so re-vendoring produces the same .jpi (verified: two runs, same sha256). It runs in the VENDOR stage, so the offline build copies the already-patched file and bit-for-bit is unaffected. CEILING: it only moves within 2.22 -- if the resolved plugin bundles Jackson outside 2.22.x and below 2.22.3 it fails the vendor stage; if upstream ships a jackson2-api with 2.22.3 or later it does nothing. The last loop fails the vendor stage if ANY vendored plugin still bundles jackson-core/databind below 2.22.3. Jenkins still reports the plugin as 2.22.2-445.vdc613f1d8012. Verified 2026-10-05 by booting chain 492's image with the patched .jpi swapped in: 63/63 plugins active, none failed, PackageVersion 2.22.3 for core/databind/yaml loaded from the plugin, ObjectMapper round trip OK. REMOVE this command once a jackson2-api release bundles 2.22.3 (it then no-ops anyway).
offline_build_cmds: cd /src && COREPACK_ENABLE_NETWORK=0 YARN_ENABLE_OFFLINE_MODE=1 mvn -o -B -am -pl war,bom -Pquick-build -Dmaven.repo.local=/m2 install
source._offline_build_cmds_note: NO `clean` IN THE OFFLINE REPLAY, AND THAT IS THE TRAP ON THIS PRODUCT. maven-clean-plugin is configured to delete .yarn/, node/, node_modules/ AND jsbundles/, and the documented build command starts with clean — so replaying it verbatim offline would wipe the vendored Yarn cache, the vendored Node and the compiled bundles immediately before the build that needs them, then fail with no network to recover. The online stage keeps clean (it runs first, and the build repopulates); the offline stage must not.
source.source_date_epoch_provenance: the time release 2.580.2-CE-ubuntu24.04-r5 was cut (2026-11-22T07:49:41Z), by scripts/retarget.py --rev-bump: ReadyStack dates an image by when its release was packaged (owner 2026-11-10), recorded here once and used by every rebuild of the release; it builds upstream commit ea3f958268fe, dated 2026-10-26T11:33:17Z (source.commit_epoch).
source._reproducibility_note: Jenkins is unusually well placed here: its own pom.xml sets project.build.outputTimestamp (2026-08-31T16:31:21Z) and the README carries a Reproducible-Builds badge, so upstream already maintains byte-reproducibility of the war. Our MAVEN_ARGS injection overrides that property with this strategy's SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which is fine and arguably better — what matters is that the ONLINE and OFFLINE stages agree, and a single injected constant guarantees they do. NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN: upstream's reproducibility check evidently runs in a setting stable enough that stapler's identity-hash-ordered .stapler output repeats; ours did not -- see _source_prep_note for the one residual and its fix.
source._version_note: jenkins-2.580.1 is the latest LTS GA (checked 2026-10-10 for r2: updates.jenkins.io/stable/latestCore.txt = 2.580.1, the newest LTS in repo.jenkins-ci.org's jenkins-war maven-metadata is 2.580.1, and jenkinsci/jenkins has no jenkins-2.580.2 tag or -rc yet; the latest WEEKLY is jenkins-2.585 and is deliberately not used — see _README). r2 is a revision release of 2.580.1. Java 17 is dead as of 2.555.1; the supported JDKs are 21 and 25.
source._offline_env_note: offline_env is emitted into BOTH stages — the renderer does that deliberately, so the warmed cache matches the replay. Which means the offline-ONLY flags must NOT live here: COREPACK_ENABLE_NETWORK=0 in the online vendor stage would stop corepack fetching the Yarn 4 bundle, and the stage whose entire job is to WARM that cache would fail with nothing to warm. They are set inline on the offline mvn invocation instead. The render caught this before the first drive did.
source._plugin_pinning_followup: CLOSED 2026-11-02. The closure is pinned: source.vendor_closures[jenkins-plugins] lists all 63 plugins with version, URL and the update centre's sha256, and the generator downloads and checks exactly those (gen_dockerfile.vendor_closure_runs); jenkins-plugin-cli and its jar are no longer used. The set is the one the published r4 (chain 681) shipped, read back from its SBOM and CHECKSUMS.sha256; every file's sha256 equals the update centre's. On 2026-11-02 the update centre offered newer releases of four members for 2.580.1 (cloudbees-folder 6.1107.v31f8955765c8, configuration-as-code 2144.ve8c697101488, joda-time-api 2.15.1-211.ve499f52b_da_33, workflow-cps 4400.v300cf4f6cef5), none listed in a security warning against the pinned versions. Jenkins core 2.580.1 itself is named by the update centre's warning core-2_588 (security advisory 2026-10-28, fixed in LTS 2.580.2): the retarget to 2.580.2 re-resolves the closure with scripts/jenkins-plugins-pin.py --resolve --core 2.580.2.
source._maven_args_extra_note: build_kit strips .git from the build context on purpose -- a git directory makes the context non-deterministic -- and jenkins' parent pom (org.jenkins-ci:jenkins) binds buildnumber-maven-plugin:create at the validate phase. With no .git the plugin fails with 'Cannot get the revision information from the scm repository' and takes the whole reactor down, killing chain 423 at build_kit after 19 minutes. It is a VENDOR/OFFLINE ASYMMETRY: the vendor stage still has the clone it created, so the same Maven command succeeds there and the problem cannot appear until the hermetic build runs. revisionOnScmFailure is the plugin's own escape hatch for this exact path -- the observed error text is the else-branch it bypasses -- and the property name was read from the 3.2.1 plugin descriptor rather than guessed. The value is the @COMMIT@ token, which gen_dockerfile expands from source.commit -- the real commit the release tag dereferences to, the same sha source_date_epoch_provenance records -- so both stages stamp an identical, truthful revision. IT WAS A LITERAL SHA UNTIL 2026-10-04 and went stale: the retarget to 2.580.1 moved source.commit but not this flag, so chain 479's war and jenkins-core.jar both carried 'Implementation-Build: 01174bc4...' -- the 2.568.3 commit -- in their manifests. retarget.py only tokenizes ldflags; a token here cannot drift. Preferred over faking a git repo in the build stage (the rabbitmq approach), which would embed a fabricated revision in the shipped artifact. NOT setting -Dmaven.buildNumber.doCheck=false: the parent pom hardcodes doCheck in its <configuration>, which overrides the property expression, and doCheck demonstrably did not fail the build -- the reactor reached the revision call.

vendor_closures.name: jenkins-plugins
vendor_closures.resolved_by: jenkins-plugin-cli 2.15.0 for the five requested plugins against Jenkins 2.580.2, in the vendor stage of the published release 2.580.1-CE-ubuntu24.04-r4 (chain 681, 2026-10-27); read back from that release's SBOM (versions) and CHECKSUMS.sha256 (files) by scripts/jenkins-plugins-pin.py --from-archive
vendor_closures.how: The vendor stage downloads each plugin from the update centre by its exact version URL, checks all 63 files against the sha256 the update centre publishes for each (plugin-versions.json, read 2026-11-02, which equals the sha256 of the file the published r4 ships) in one `sha256sum -c`, and fails unless /plugins holds exactly those 63 files. scripts/jenkins-plugins-pin.py --verify also checks that every plugin each member needs is in the set at the version it needs or newer, and that none needs a newer Jenkins than 2.580.2.
vendor_closures._note: The plugins the image ships: the five requested ones and everything they need (63 in all). Until 2026-11-02 the vendor stage ran jenkins-plugin-cli with the five names and no versions, so the set was whatever the update centre served newest that day (strategy `_plugin_pinning_followup`, now closed). This is the set the published r4 shipped, so the next build re-creates its plugins byte for byte; to move it, run scripts/jenkins-plugins-pin.py --resolve --write (and check the update centre's security warnings).
